entries.title: Unitree Go2
entries.content:
Unitree Go2

go2_calibration

go2_calibration measures how the lidar and the IMU are mounted on the Unitree Go2. It writes the result into a ROS 2 parameter file, and go2_preprocessor reads that file.

What. One program (ros2 run go2_calibration go2_calibration). The robot stands still, spins and tilts for about 97 s while the program records its sensors. Then it computes a few numbers:

- where the lidar sits on the body, and how it is rotated;
- the bias and the scale error of the body IMU;
- how much too long the lidar measures every distance.

Why. Point-LIO builds the map from the lidar cloud and the IMU. Both must be in the same frame, the body frame, and their numbers must be right. A wrong rotation bends the whole map.

Nothing is typed into the code. CMU’s calibrate_imu keeps the lidar rotation of its own robot in the code. On our firmware that rotation is wrong by about 25 deg, and their method cannot see it. Here every rotation is measured, and every result is checked. If one check fails, no file is written, so a bad calibration cannot reach the map by accident.

When. Once per robot. Again after a firmware update, after the lidar was remounted, or after a hard fall.

Where it sits



tools/mapping/calibration.sh is the easy way to run it. It records the bag, runs the program, and points ~/calibration/current.yaml at the new file. map.sh then uses that link.

What it measures

lidar_to_bodyFloor tiltrange_offsetbody_imu.gyro_biasbody_imu.accel_scaleBody gravity directionimu_to_bodyLidar IMU gyro_bias, gyro_leak, gravityResultRotation and position of the lidar on the bodyHow tilted the floor looks after lidar_to_body. This checks lidar_to_body by other meansThe lidar measures every distance this much too longWhat the body gyroscope shows when still9.81 divided by what the still body accelerometer readsIs the still accelerometer pointing up?Rotation from the lidar IMU to the bodySame kind of numbers for the lidar IMUWhat it means/utlidar/cloud against its body-frame copy /utlidar/cloud_base, robot stillThe floor in the raw cloudHow the flat floor bends into a bowl/sportmodestate, robot still/sportmodestate, robot still/sportmodestate, robot stillBoth gyroscopes while the robot turns and tiltsLidar IMUTaken fromyesno, check onlyyesyesyesno, check onlyno, report onlyno, report onlyWritten to the file

go2_preprocessor gives Point-LIO the body IMU only. The lidar IMU results stay as comments in the file, but their checks still count: one failure stops the file. The angle between imu_to_body and lidar_to_body tells whether the body IMU axes agree with the lidar mount (0.65 deg on our Go2).

Quick start

On the robot, on a flat floor with 1 m free around it:

	tools/mapping/calibration.sh

By hand:

	source ~/unitree_ros2/setup.sh
	source ~/unitree_go2/install/setup.bash
	ros2 run go2_calibration go2_calibration

Without moving anything, from a recorded bag (it must contain /calibration/phase):

	ros2 run go2_calibration go2_calibration --ros-args -p bag:=<bag folder> -p output:=<file>

Use the result with go2_preprocessor --ros-args --params-file go2_calibration.yaml.

How it works

The code in one picture

The program is a straight line: read settings, fill a buffer, calibrate, report, write the file. Two sources can fill the buffer, the live robot or a bag. Both make the same calls, so calibrate() never knows where the data came from.

An arrow means “uses”.



Everything in the core box is plain C++ with Eigen (a matrix library). It has no ROS and is unit tested. The ros box is thin: it only reads and writes messages.

A live run, step by step



main.cpp in four steps:

1. Settings. Every setting is a ROS parameter with a default. build_sequence rejects a value out of range before anything moves.
2. Fill the buffer. Live: warn, count down 5 s (Ctrl-C cancels, nothing moves), run_live. Bag: read_bag.
3. Calibrate and print. calibrate() throws a clear error if data is missing (no floor, no turning, no still sample).
4. Write. Only if every check passed. The exit code is 0 only then.

The motion

The live source runs ten phases. A phase has a name, a length and one sport command.



stillspin_left, spin_righttilt_pitch, tilt_rollpause, balance_stand, levelPhaseStopMoveMove(0, 0, +1 or -1 rad/s), 2 turns eachEuler, 0.2 rad sine at 0.4 HzStopMove, BalanceStand (sent once), Euler(0, 0, 0)CommandstillmovingmovingnoneSample useBias, lidar mount, floor, range offset need a robot that does not moveThe two IMUs must see the same rotationTurns about the other two axes. Turns alone leave those axes unknownTransitions. Their samples are droppedWhy

The length of a spin is turns * 2 * pi / rate = 2 * 6.283 / 1.0 = 12.57 s. All phases together: 30 + 12.57 + 3 + 12.57 + 3 + 1 + 15 + 15 + 2 + 3 = 97.1 s. With motion.tilt_angle:=0 the tilts are left out and the run is 61.1 s.

The phase name is also the label of the samples. use_of(name) is the only place that decides: still is still, names starting with spin_ or tilt_ are moving, anything else is dropped. The live source publishes the name on /calibration/phase at 50 Hz, so a bag recorded alongside can be replayed later.

The live source and its safety

run_live has three parts: subscribe, wait for the sensors, run the phases.



Safety rules, all in this loop:

- Nothing moves until all four sensor topics have sent a message.
- Every way out sends StopMove for 0.5 s: the end, Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, a silent robot and any exception. main handles Ctrl-C itself, because rclcpp’s own handler would shut ROS down before the robot got its StopMove.
- Speed and angle have hard limits (1.5 rad/s, 0.3 rad, 1 Hz). No parameter can go above them.
- Commands go out at 50 Hz, like Unitree’s examples. The loop itself spins at 1000 Hz. At 50 Hz it kept only 1 IMU sample in 5, and each was old.
- Samples get their receive time: it is the only clock both IMUs share. A bag stores the same receive time, so live and bag give the same data.



The bag source

read_bag replays a recorded bag, message by message, into the buffer. It makes the same calls as the live source. It opens the bag, checks that all five topics are in it (the four sensors plus /calibration/phase), then:



A cloud is only decoded if wants_scans() is true. Decoding is the slow part.

The buffer

CalibrationBuffer sorts every sample into a box, depending on the current phase.



set_phase only counts a change of name, because the live source repeats it 50 times a second.

Matching the two clouds. The firmware publishes every scan twice: /utlidar/cloud in the lidar frame and /utlidar/cloud_base in the body frame. Both carry the same stamp. The copy that arrives first waits in a map. When the second arrives, the points are paired by a key of (time, intensity, ring):



Example, made-up numbers: the point with key (t=0.0123, intensity=40, ring=3) is at (1.0, 0.2, -0.3) in the lidar scan and at (-0.3, 1.0, -0.2) in the body scan. They become one pair. A key that appears twice in one scan is skipped, because it cannot be told apart. The buffer keeps at most max_scans (100) matched scans, only while the robot is still. A phase change throws away scans still waiting for a partner.

The calibration

calibrate(data, limits) is a pure function: numbers in, numbers out. It has six steps.



1. Lidar mount and floor

Lidar mount. The paired points are the same physical points in two frames. The best rotation R and shift t that carry the first set onto the second is found with the Kabsch method:

1. subtract the centre of each point set;
2. add up from * to^T for all pairs, a 3x3 table;
3. its SVD (a standard matrix split, U S V^T) gives the rotation R = V U^T. If that turns out to be a mirror image (determinant -1), one axis is flipped;
4. t = centre_to - R * centre_from.

The error is the rms (typical size) of the distance left over. Result on our Go2: error 0.000 mm, because the firmware used the same transform to make the copy.

That is why the next step exists: the mount comes from the firmware’s own copy, so it is not an independent measurement. The floor is.

Floor. find_floor uses RANSAC:

1. take 3 random points, make a plane through them;
2. keep it only if it is 0.2 to 0.7 m from the lidar (the floor, not a wall);
3. count the points within 3 cm of it;
4. repeat 600 times, keep the plane with most points;
5. refit that plane through all its points by least squares.

The random seed is fixed, so every run gives the same answer. At most 40000 points are used. Then the floor normal is turned by lidar_to_body. If the mount is right it points straight up, and the floor tilt is the angle to +z. Real value on our Go2: 0.82 deg (limit 2 deg).

Range offset. If every distance is too long by o, a flat floor looks like a bowl. A point whose ray hits the floor at angle a from the vertical appears at h + o * cos(a) instead of h. fit_range_offset fits h and o by least squares. Example from the formula: with h = 0.33 m and o = 0.11 m, the point straight below reads 0.44 m deep, and a point at 60 deg reads 0.33 + 0.11 * 0.5 = 0.385 m. Real result on our Go2: o = 0.110 m.

2. Body IMU, robot still

- gyro_bias = the mean of the still gyroscope. Its std (spread) is the noise.
- accel_scale = 9.81 / length of the mean accelerometer. It is a scale and not a bias: standing still shows only the reading along gravity, and there a scale and a bias look the same. Real value: the still accelerometer reads 9.43 m/s^2, so accel_scale = 9.81 / 9.43 = 1.040.
- Body tilt = angle between the mean accelerometer and +z.

3. Lidar IMU rotation (report only)

fit_imu_rotation matches the lidar IMU gyroscope to the body gyroscope with the same Kabsch fit, but only for samples where the robot really turns (rate at least 0.15 rad/s). Both IMUs have a different clock delay, so it tries every lag from -100 ms to +100 ms in 5 ms steps. For each lag it pairs each sample with the nearest one (at most 3 ms away), fits, and keeps the lag with the smallest error. A live run on 2026-10-19 found -40 ms.

The axis spread tells whether the robot turned about more than one axis. It is the second largest over the largest eigenvalue of the rates’ spread matrix. Spinning on the spot only turns about z, and then the rotation about z cannot be told. The tilts add the other two axes.

4. Lidar IMU bias and gravity

The still lidar gyroscope and accelerometer are rotated into the body frame with imu_to_body. The mean gyroscope is the lidar IMU gyro_bias. The mean accelerometer against +z gives the gravity tilt. It is synthetic on the Go2 (154 deg on ours), which is why the lidar IMU is not used.

5. Leak

When the robot turns on the spot, a perfect gyroscope shows nothing on x and y. fit_leak measures the share of the yaw rate that still shows there. Made-up example: yaw rate z = 1.0 rad/s and x reads 0.03, so z_to_x = -0.03. The correction would be x += z_to_x * z.

6. Checks

Each check is one value against one limit. The defaults are what our Go2 gave on 2026-10-13, with a wide margin.

Body gyroscope noiseBody accel_scale errorBody gravity tiltMatched lidar pointslidar_to_body error rmsFloor tilt after lidar_to_bodyimu_to_body error rmsimu_to_body lagTurn axis spreadStill lidar gyroscope noisegyro_leak leftCheckat most 0.02 rad/sat most 0.1at most 5 degat least 1000at most 1 mmat most 2 degat most 0.25 rad/sat most 95 msat least 0.01at most 0.02 rad/sat most 0.1Limit0.0070.041.2 to 2.21515770.0000.820.120.040.0070.034Value on our Go2

The lag limit is 95 ms and not 100: a lag on the edge of the search means the best lag is outside.

The report and the file

describe(calibration) makes one line per result and one per check (PASS or FAIL). The terminal and the comments at the top of the file show the same lines. to_parameter_file writes the YAML. Numbers are always written with a decimal point and never as 1e-05: the ROS parameter reader would take 1 for an integer and 1e-05 for a string, and an array must not mix types.

Types and files



sequencebufferfittingfloorimu_fitcalibratereportmessagesbag_sourcelive_sourcemainFilePhases, the command at each moment, which phases are still or movingCalibrationBuffer: samples sorted by phase, scans matched with their copyKabsch rotation fit (vectors) and rigid fit (points)RANSAC floor plane, tilt from +z, range offsetPairing by time, IMU rotation with lag search, axis spread, statistics, leakThe whole calibration and its checksThe report lines and the parameter fileTopic names, message conversions, sport requestsread_bag(): a bag into the bufferrun_live(): drives the robot and fills the bufferSettings, the linear flow, Ctrl-CDoesnononononononoyesyesyesyesROS

CMake builds the ROS-free files as go2_calibration_core, the others as go2_calibration_ros. The executable and the tests link them. messages.cpp also turns a Command into the Unitree request (Move and Euler carry {"x":..,"y":..,"z":..} as JSON, the API ids are 1002 BalanceStand, 1003 StopMove, 1007 Euler, 1008 Move).

Parameters

All are ROS parameters (-p name:=value or --params-file). The defaults suit any Go2 with the L1.

bagoutputnode_namemax_scanstopics.cloud, topics.cloud_base, topics.imutopics.body_state, topics.request, topics.phasemotion.still_s, motion.pause_smotion.spin_rate, motion.spin_turnsmotion.tilt_angle, motion.tilt_frequency, motion.tilt_slimits.*Parameteremptygo2_calibration.yamlgo2_preprocessor100/utlidar/cloud, /utlidar/cloud_base, /utlidar/imu/sportmodestate, /api/sport/request, /calibration/phase30, 31.0, 20.2, 0.4, 15the table in “Checks”DefaultEmpty: live run. A bag folder: calibrate from itThe file writtenThe node the file is for (its top-level key)Matched scans kept for the lidar mountLidar cloud, its body-frame copy, lidar IMUBody IMU, sport commands, phase names. Range 10 to 300 and 1 to 30rad/s (0.3 to 1.5), turns each way (0.5 to 5)rad (0 to 0.3, 0 skips the tilts), Hz (0.1 to 1), s (2 to 60)min_matched_points, max_mount_error_mm, max_floor_tilt_deg, max_gyro_error, min_axis_spread, max_still_noise, max_leak, max_accel_scale_error, max_body_tilt_degMeaning

A motion value outside its range stops the program before anything moves.

Output

	# Go2 calibration for go2_preprocessor, written by go2_calibration on <date>
	# from <bag or "a live run">.
	# ... the report and the checks, as comments ...
	go2_preprocessor:
	  ros__parameters:
	    lidar_to_body:
	      rotation: [9 values, row-major]
	      translation: [x, y, z]
	    body_imu:
	      gyro_bias: {x, y, z}
	      accel_scale: <about 1.04>
	    range_offset: <metres>

Convention: p_body = R * p_sensor + t, R row-major, body frame x forward, y left, z up. The body IMU needs no rotation: /sportmodestate already uses the body axes.



Build and test

The package needs Unitree’s unitree_api and unitree_go messages. On the robot they come with ~/unitree_ros2:

	cd ~/unitree_go2
	source ~/unitree_ros2/setup.sh
	colcon build --packages-select go2_calibration
	colcon test --packages-select go2_calibration && colcon test-result --verbose

Laptop (foxy container), once: sudo apt install ros-foxy-rosidl-generator-dds-idl, clone https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_ros2, build only the messages (cd unitree_ros2/cyclonedds_ws && colcon build --packages-select unitree_api unitree_go), and source cyclonedds_ws/install/local_setup.bash after /opt/ros/foxy/setup.bash.

Tests cover every ROS-free file, the message conversions, and the bag source (on bags the tests write). The live source drives a robot and has no unit test. It was checked on the laptop against fake topics on an isolated domain (ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1 ROS_DOMAIN_ID=77): no robot, a full run, and Ctrl-C in the middle of a turn.

Results on our Go2

Real numbers.

2026-10-13, bags calib, standstill and spin merged with phase messages (all checks PASS):

- lidar_to_body = R_y(165 deg) R_z(-123 deg), t = (0.282, 0, 0), error rms 0.000 mm.
- Floor tilt 0.82 deg. range_offset 0.110 m, lidar 0.330 m above the floor.
- imu_to_body is 0.65 deg from lidar_to_body: the lidar IMU gyroscope uses the cloud’s axes.
- Lidar IMU gyro_bias (0.0028, -0.0055, 0.0006) rad/s. Gravity 154 deg from +z after imu_to_body.

2026-10-19, three live calibrations, body IMU:

- accel_scale 1.0385 to 1.0420. The still accelerometer reads 9.41 to 9.45 m/s^2.
- Gravity 1.2 to 2.2 deg from +z. Gyro bias about (-0.010, 0.011, -0.004) rad/s.
- Only calibration_03 passed every check. The other two failed the floor tilt (2.05 and 2.83 deg), and calibration_02 also the still noise.

Known gaps

- range_offset may depend on the distance. go2_preprocessor subtracts one constant from every range. Over all floor points it is 0.110 m. Over the floor within 1.6 m only, an earlier analysis gave 0.128 m. Check it against a wall at taped distances.
- The lidar mount is the firmware’s value, not an independent measurement. The floor tilt is the only independent check.
- A bag needs /calibration/phase. Old bags without it must be merged with phase messages first.
- The lidar accelerometer is synthetic, so the gravity direction of the lidar IMU is reported and never used.

entries.title: Unitree Go2
entries.content:
Unitree Go2

go2_preprocessor

go2_preprocessor turns the raw Go2 lidar cloud and body IMU into what Point-LIO expects: both in the body frame, corrected with the numbers from go2_calibration.

What. One ROS 2 node (ros2 run go2_preprocessor go2_preprocessor). It runs while you map. It listens to the raw lidar cloud and to the robot state, fixes both with the calibration file, and publishes two clean topics for Point-LIO:

- the cloud, moved into the body frame, with the ranges shortened and the robot’s own points removed;
- the body IMU, with the gyroscope bias removed and the accelerometer scaled to 9.81.

Why. Point-LIO builds the map from a cloud and an IMU. They must share one frame and tell the truth. The raw Go2 data does neither:

- the cloud is in the lidar frame, and the lidar is mounted upside down and tilted;
- every lidar range reads about 0.11 m too long;
- the body IMU has a bias, and a still accelerometer reads 9.44 m/s^2 instead of 9.81;
- the lidar sees the robot’s own back.

Fed raw, Point-LIO draws a tilted and stretched map.

When. Every time you map. It is the first node of the mapping chain, and mapping.launch.py starts it.

Where it sits



The measured numbers (lidar_to_body, body_imu, range_offset) come from the go2_calibration file. The robot box is written by hand in preprocessor.yaml. The lidar’s own IMU (/utlidar/imu) is not used: its accelerometer is synthetic.

What it changes

Cloud, every rangeCloud, every pointCloud, robot’s own pointsIMU, gyroscopeIMU, accelerometerIMU, repeated samplesDataMoves each point back towards the lidar. A point closer than the offset is droppedTurns it from the lidar frame into the body frame: p_body = R * p_lidar + tDrops the points inside a box around the robot’s back (body frame)Subtracts the still biasMultiplies by the scale that makes a still reading 9.81Drops a sample whose stamp is not newer than the last oneWhat the node doesrange_offsetlidar_to_body.*robot_box.*body_imu.gyro_bias.*body_imu.accel_scalenoneParameter

Intensity, ring and time of each point, and the stamp of the cloud, pass through unchanged.

Quick start

With the whole mapping chain (preprocessor, Point-LIO, map builder):

	ros2 launch go2_mapping_bringup mapping.launch.py calibration_file:=$HOME/calibration/current.yaml

tools/mapping/map.sh starts the same chain with the current calibration. The node alone:

	ros2 run go2_preprocessor go2_preprocessor --ros-args \
	    --params-file src/go2_mapping_bringup/config/preprocessor.yaml \
	    --params-file $HOME/calibration/current.yaml

The node name must stay go2_preprocessor: both files are keyed by it, and a different name makes ROS ignore them without an error.

How it works

The code in one picture

Everything is one executable. The files in the box are plain C++ with Eigen (a matrix library), except the node, which needs ROS. An arrow means “uses”.



Start-up

The node reads every setting once, when it starts. All of them are read-only parameters: a later ros2 param set fails with an error instead of being silently ignored.



rotation_from_parameter refuses a matrix that is not a rotation (stretched axes, or a mirror image), so a typo in the file stops the node at start-up. The log line calibration: shows whether the file was applied: look for your numbers there.

A cloud message



The order matters. The robot box is written in the body frame, so the points are turned before the box is applied. The ranges are shortened first because the offset belongs to the lidar: it is measured along each ray from the lidar’s centre. A cloud that cannot be read (data shorter than its declared size, or a missing field) is logged and skipped.

Example. Real run of the actual code, with the calibration of 2026-10-19 (lidar_to_body and range_offset 0.1129 m). The points are made up: they were computed back from a known place in the body frame, with every range 0.1129 m too long, the way the lidar reads them.

wallfloorrobot’s backPoint(2.000, 0.500, -0.100)(0.800, -0.200, -0.320)(-0.400, 0.000, -0.250)True place in the body frame(0.500, -1.746, 0.575), 1.905 m(0.465, -0.284, 0.521), 0.754 m(-0.455, 0.701, 0.075), 0.839 mWhat the lidar reads (lidar frame)(2.108, 0.532, -0.106)(0.891, -0.235, -0.376)dropped, inside the boxWithout range_offset(2.000, 0.500, -0.100)(0.800, -0.200, -0.320)dropped, inside the boxWith range_offset 0.1129

Without the correction the wall sits 11 cm too far and the floor 5.6 cm too low.

An IMU message



1 to 1.5 % of the messages repeat the previous sample, with the same stamp and the same values. Point-LIO would take the copy as one more measurement at the same instant, so the node drops it.

The stamp is the one inside the message, which uses the lidar’s clock, and not the receive time. The orientation and the covariances stay at their defaults (“unknown”): Point-LIO reads only the rates and the acceleration.

Example. The body IMU at rest on our Go2: the accelerometer reads (-0.146, -0.133, 9.444), with length 9.446. The scale 9.81 / 9.446 = 1.0385 turns it into (-0.152, -0.138, 9.808). The small sideways parts grow by the same factor, because it is a scale and not a bias.

Types



mainpreprocessor_nodeconvertorrobot_utilsimu_transformcalibrationschemasFileStarts the node and spinsThe two callbacks, the parameters and the topicsPointCloud2 message to PointCloud and backshorten_ranges, lidar_to_body, remove_robot_points, preprocess_cloudcalibrate_gyro and calibrate_accelTurns the parameter numbers into a rotation and a vector, and checks themPoint, PointCloud and Box (contains uses strict limits)Does

Parameters

All are read-only ROS parameters, read once at start-up.

lidar_to_body.rotationlidar_to_body.translationbody_imu.gyro_bias.x, .y, .zbody_imu.accel_scalerange_offsetrobot_box.min_x, max_xrobot_box.min_y, max_yrobot_box.min_z, max_zParameterCMU’s mount(0, 0, -0.046825)01.00-0.7, -0.1-0.3, 0.3-0.646825, -0.046825Default9 numbers, row-major. Must be a rotationm, 3 numbersrad/s, subtracted from the gyroscopemultiplies the accelerometerm, subtracted from every lidar rangem, body framemmMeaning

A name that is not in the table is not an error: ROS ignores it, and the default is used. Check the calibration: log line.

Topics

ininoutoutDirection/utlidar/cloud/sportmodestate/utlidar/transformed_cloud/utlidar/transformed_imuTopicsensor_msgs/PointCloud2unitree_go/SportModeStatesensor_msgs/PointCloud2, frame bodysensor_msgs/Imu, frame bodyTypesensor data QoSsensor data QoS1050Queue

The topic names are fixed in the code. The output IMU queue is deeper because the IMU is much faster than the lidar.

Build and test

Needs Unitree’s unitree_go messages. On the robot they come with ~/unitree_ros2:

	cd ~/unitree_go2
	source ~/unitree_ros2/setup.sh
	colcon build --packages-select go2_preprocessor
	colcon test --packages-select go2_preprocessor && colcon test-result --verbose

Four test programs, one per file: test_convertor (round trip and layout), test_schemas (the box limits), test_robot_utils (turn, filter, and both in order), test_imu_transform. Each one compiles the file it tests again, because the code lives in the executable and not in a library.

Known gaps

- The box is still CMU’s. robot_box was made for CMU’s lidar_to_body translation (0, 0, -0.046825). Ours is (0.282, 0, 0). The comment in preprocessor.yaml says to check it in RViz with the real calibration. Not done yet.
- No calibration file means CMU’s mount. Started alone without a calibration file, the node uses CMU’s rotation and no IMU correction, and the map comes out tilted. mapping.launch.py requires calibration_file, but ros2 run does not. Only the start-up log shows it.
- calibration.cpp has no unit test. It is what stops a stretched or mirrored rotation, and the wrong number of values. The four test programs do not include it. shorten_ranges has none yet either.
- The log line counts range drops as robot points. robot points removed is points in minus points out, so it also counts the points dropped for being closer than range_offset.

entries.title: Unitree Go2
entries.content:
Unitree Go2

go2_mapping_bringup

go2_mapping_bringup starts the mapping chain. It has no code: only launch files that start the nodes, and config files that hold their settings.

What. A ROS 2 package with three launch files and three config files. One command starts go2_preprocessor, Point-LIO and map_builder, gives each its settings, and connects them with the right topic names.

Why. The chain has three programs from three places, and they only work together if the details match:

- each one needs its own settings file, and a wrong node name makes ROS ignore the file without an error;
- Point-LIO reads the preprocessor’s topics, and map_builder reads Point-LIO’s topics;
- the calibration file must reach the preprocessor, or the map comes out tilted;
- the robot and the laptop must use the same DDS (the layer ROS uses to send messages), or they do not see each other.

This package fixes all of these in one place, so nobody types them by hand.

When. Every time you map. tools/mapping/map.sh calls it for you.

Where it sits



The package does not run anything itself. It tells ROS what to start. The three nodes it starts have their own pages: go2_preprocessor and map_builder.

What is inside

launch/mapping.launch.pylaunch/map_builder.launch.pylaunch/laptop.launch.pyconfig/preprocessor.yamlconfig/point_lio.yamlconfig/map_builder.yamlCMakeLists.txtpackage.xmlFileThe main one. Starts the preprocessor and Point-LIO, and map_builder when it runs on the robotStarts map_builder alone. Included by the other two, not run by handThe laptop side. Starts map_builder there when you want it thereThe robot box of go2_preprocessorAll settings of Point-LIOVoxel size and publish rates of map_builderInstalls launch/ and config/ so ROS can find themLists the four packages it starts as run dependenciesDoes

Quick start

The normal way, on the robot computer. The script checks the topics, the disk and the calibration, and then calls the launch file:

	tools/mapping/map.sh

The launch file alone:

	ros2 launch go2_mapping_bringup mapping.launch.py \
	    calibration_file:=$HOME/calibration/current.yaml

calibration_file has no default. This is on purpose: without it the preprocessor would use CMU’s mount values, and the map would come out tilted. Launch stops at once if you forget it.

The same command works live and with ros2 bag play. All nodes use the stamps inside the messages and not the clock, so there is no use_sim_time switch (Foxy’s bag player has no --clock).

How it works

Who starts whom

mapping.launch.py is a list of actions. ROS runs them in order. The last one includes another launch file, but only when a condition is true.



Both mapping.launch.py and laptop.launch.py include map_builder.launch.py. One of them has the condition true, the other false, so map_builder starts exactly once. Step 3 is explained in Which DDS.

What happens at start-up



The three nodes start together, not one after the other. Nothing waits for the previous node to be ready. This is fine because a node that has no input yet just waits.

Point-LIO needs about 3 s to start, then it takes gravity and its first map from the next seconds. The robot must stand still for that time. map.sh prints KEEP THE ROBOT STILL for 10 s.

Where the data flows

The launch files do not carry data. They only set the names so that the nodes find each other.



Where the names are set:

Go2 to preprocessorPreprocessor to Point-LIOPoint-LIO to map_builderConnectiongo2_preprocessor codepoint_lio.yamlmap_builder.launch.pySet inFixed in the codelid_topic and imu_topicremappings: cloud becomes /cloud_registered, odom becomes /aft_mapped_to_initHow

map_builder only knows the short names cloud and odom. The launch file points them at Point-LIO. The frame of /cloud_registered is camera_init, Point-LIO’s world frame.

How the settings reach each node



Each file starts with a key: the node name. ROS gives the file to the node with that name and ignores it for all others. If the key and the name differ, ROS says nothing and the node runs with its defaults. This is why the launch file comments say “the node name must stay go2_preprocessor”.

For the preprocessor two files are given. The second wins when both set a value. The robot box is in preprocessor.yaml and the measured numbers are in the calibration file, so they never clash.

output_dir is not in map_builder.yaml. The launch file sets it, because ~ must mean the home folder of the machine that runs the node, and that is only known at launch time.

Robot or laptop

By default everything runs on the robot. You can move map_builder to the laptop. Point-LIO then sends its scans over Wi-Fi.



	# on the robot
	ros2 launch go2_mapping_bringup mapping.launch.py calibration_file:=... map_builder_host:=laptop
	# on the laptop
	ros2 launch go2_mapping_bringup laptop.launch.py map_builder_host:=laptop

The value must be the same on both machines. Two commands that say robot and laptop would start two map_builders (the second stops itself) or none. On the laptop with robot, the launch starts nothing.

Which DDS

DDS is the layer under ROS that sends the messages. Foxy uses Fast-RTPS by default. The robot uses CycloneDDS. Two machines with different DDS do not talk to each other. Point-LIO also hangs on Ctrl-C with Fast-RTPS.

Both launch files therefore set RMW_IMPLEMENTATION to rmw_cyclonedds_cpp, but only if the shell has no value yet. A value you set yourself is kept.

What happens on Ctrl-C



Ctrl-C reaches every node. map_builder writes the map into a new folder <output_dir>/<time of the first scan, UTC>/. The Point-LIO message is a known flaw of its exit. It comes after the map is saved and does not cost data.

The settings

Launch arguments

calibration_filemap_builder_hostoutput_dirArgumentnone, requiredrobot~/mapsDefaultmapping.launch.pymapping.launch.py, laptop.launch.pymap_builder.launch.pyInAbsolute path of the go2_calibration outputWhich machine runs map_builder. Same on bothFolder where each run gets its sub-folderMeaning

output_dir is declared in map_builder.launch.py. Passed to mapping.launch.py it reaches it.

point_lio.yaml

Taken from CMU’s utlidar.yaml. The file has about 60 values, each with a comment. These are the ones that differ from CMU or that you may want to change:

lid_topic, imu_topicextrinsic_T, extrinsic_Rinit_map_sizegravity, gravity_alignacc_normsatu_accblindfilter_size_surf, filter_size_mapuse_imu_as_inputpcd_save_enParameterthe preprocessor’s two topicszero, identity5000(0, 0, -9.81), true9.81400.5 m0.1 mfalsefalseValuePoint-LIO reads the corrected data, not the robot’sThe preprocessor already turned lidar and IMU into one body frameAbout 0.5 s of scans. CMU’s 10 builds the first map from one scan, mostly floor, and the gyro bias runs awayThe IMU is scaled to 9.81 at rest. Without gravity, Point-LIO reads it as the robot speeding upThe accelerometer unit is m/s^2The body accelerometer peaks at 29 m/s^2 at foot strikes. CMU’s 30 would flag themDrops lidar points closer than this. It removes the robot’s own bodyVoxel size of the scan and of Point-LIO’s map. Smaller means finer, more memory and CPUThe IMU is a measurement of the filter, which holds up in rough motionPoint-LIO would overwrite one file per run. map_builder saves each run in its own folderWhy

map_builder.yaml

voxel_sizedelta_rate_hzpose_rate_hzfull_map_rate_hzsave_on_exitParameter0.05 m2100trueValueOne point per voxel. On 2026-10-19_line_01: 45,195 points at 0.05, 14,476 at 0.10How often new voxels are sentHow often the robot pose is sentThe whole map on a topic. 0 is off, because every message holds the whole mapSave on Ctrl-C, so a run is not lost if nobody called the save serviceMeaning

Calling the save service and then stopping gives two folders, <time> and <time>_1.

preprocessor.yaml

Only the robot_box. See go2_preprocessor for what the box does.

Build and test

The package only copies files. Build it with everything it starts:

	cd ~/unitree_go2
	source ~/unitree_ros2/setup.sh
	vcs import src < go2.repos
	colcon build --packages-up-to go2_mapping_bringup

vcs import fetches Point-LIO, pinned to one commit in go2.repos. There are no tests. A launch file has no logic worth a unit test, and the full run is tried by map.sh on a bag.

Known gaps

- No test for the launch files. A typo in a node name or a topic is found only by running the chain. The last full run was on the laptop with a bag (2026-10-19_line_01), not on the robot.
- map_builder_host must match by hand. Nothing checks that the two machines have the same value. map_builder stops a second copy of itself, but a wrong pair that starts none is not noticed.
- The robot box is still CMU’s. See go2_preprocessor.
- The RMW_IMPLEMENTATION default hides a mismatch. A shell with rmw_fastrtps_cpp already set is kept, and the two machines then do not see each other, with no error.
- laptop.launch.py starts nothing with robot. It is there for the viewer bridge, which is not written yet.

entries.title: Unitree Go2
entries.content:
Unitree Go2

map_builder

map_builder collects Point-LIO’s output into one map and one path, and saves both to disk.

What. One ROS 2 node (ros2 run map_builder map_builder). It listens to the scans and the poses that Point-LIO publishes. It keeps the scans in a voxel map: space is cut into small cubes, and each cube holds one point. It also keeps every pose, in a list. It publishes the new cubes while you map, and on Ctrl-C it writes map.pcd and trajectory.tum.

Why. Point-LIO sends the same wall again with every scan, about 10 times a second. Saved as they come, the points would pile up and the file would be huge. Point-LIO also does not save anything by default. map_builder removes the repeats and keeps the result, so a walk ends with two small files that the rest of the thesis can use.

When. Every time you map. mapping.launch.py starts it, on the robot or on the laptop.

Where it sits



The inputs are called cloud and odom inside the node. go2_mapping_bringup points them at Point-LIO’s two topics. The frame of the scans is camera_init, Point-LIO’s world frame: the origin is where the robot stood at the start, and x points where it looked.

What it does

Each scanEach poseNew cubesThe whole mapOn saveDataPuts every point in a cube. A cube that is already full ignores the new pointAppends it to the path. A pose that is not newer than the last one is skippedSends them as a delta twice a secondOn request: a service answers with every point. Or on a topic, if you turn it onWrites the map as a PCD file and the path as a TUM fileWhat the node does

Quick start

With the whole chain, which is the normal way:

	tools/mapping/map.sh

The node alone, if Point-LIO runs elsewhere:

	ros2 run map_builder map_builder --ros-args \
	    --params-file src/go2_mapping_bringup/config/map_builder.yaml \
	    -p output_dir:=$HOME/maps \
	    -r cloud:=/cloud_registered -r odom:=/aft_mapped_to_init

Save in the middle of a run, without stopping:

	ros2 service call /map_builder/save std_srvs/srv/Trigger

The answer holds the folder name. A run is written to <output_dir>/<time of the first scan, UTC>/, for example ~/maps/2026-10-19T14:35:23/.

How it works

The code in one picture

The code is split in three parts, so that the maths does not need ROS and a test does not need PCL. An arrow means “uses”.



voxel_count is a small program with no ROS. It loads a PCD file and puts it in a voxel map twice. The second time nothing must be added: it proves that no two saved points share a cube.

Start-up

All the parameters are read-only: a later ros2 param set fails with an error.



The run_id tells a viewer that a new map has begun. The check after 2 s is there because two map_builders on the same topics would send two different maps, and a viewer cannot tell them apart.

A cloud message



A cloud that cannot be read (its data is shorter than width * height * point_step, or a field is missing) is logged and skipped. The first scan fixes the map frame and the name of the save folder. Every log line “Voxels N, added M points from cloud” comes at most every 2 s.

The voxel map

VoxelMap::insert does this for every point. A point that is not a number (NaN or infinity) is skipped.



floor, not a plain cast, because a cast rounds towards 0 and puts -0.03 and +0.03 in the same cube. The map is a hash map (unordered_map) with the key hashed from three large primes, a method called spatial hashing.

Example. The numbers are made up. The voxel size is 0.05 m.

(1.23, -0.03, 0.51)(1.24, -0.04, 0.52)(1.26, -0.03, 0.51)Point (x, y, z)24.6, -0.6, 10.224.8, -0.8, 10.425.2, -0.6, 10.2x, y, z divided by 0.05(24, -1, 10)(24, -1, 10)(25, -1, 10)Keynew, storedsame cube, ignorednew, storedResult

The first point of a cube wins. It is not averaged with the later ones.

Real numbers. On the straight walk 2026-10-19_line_01 (5.4 m), voxel 0.05 m gives about 44,700 points. Voxel 0.10 m gave 14,476 points on the same walk, and 0.05 m gave 45,195 on an earlier run.

An odometry message and the three timers

Nothing is sent from the callbacks. They only store. Three timers send what was stored.



The delta holds only the new cubes, one point each, so it stays small. seq counts 1, 2, 3 and so on inside one run. stamp is the newest scan inside the delta. A delta with no new points is not sent, so a still robot sends nothing.

How a viewer keeps in step

A viewer can join late or miss a message. The rules are in the message files MapDelta.msg and GetMap.srv.



get_map first sends the pending points as a delta. This way the snapshot matches seq exactly, and the viewer never has a hole between the snapshot and the next delta.

Save



Saving twice in one run gives two folders, <time> and <time>_1. Save fails with map is empty if no scan came, and with output_dir is not set if the node has no output folder. A failed save at exit is logged and does not crash the node.

Types



mainnodecloud_msgvoxel_maptrajectorymap_iovoxel_countFileStarts the node, spins, then calls save_at_exitThe two callbacks, the timers, the services, the single-instance checkPointCloud2 message to a list of Point and backPoint, VoxelKey, the hash, and VoxelMap with insert, last_voxel_points_added, allPose, and Trajectory with add and write_tumThe run folder name, the PCD writer, the TUM writerOffline check of a PCD file, not part of the nodeDoes

The message types are in the small package go2_mapping_msgs: MapDelta.msg (header, run_id, seq, a PointCloud2 of the new points) and GetMap.srv (no request, answers with run_id, seq and a PointCloud2 of all points).

Output files

map.pcd has one point per cube, binary, fields x y z intensity, in metres, frame camera_init.

trajectory.tum has one line per pose: stamp x y z qx qy qz qw. The stamp is in seconds with 9 digits after the dot. Example line, made up:

	1760884523.123456789 1.204300 -0.031200 0.002100 0.000100 -0.002300 0.014000 0.999900

The path starts at (0, 0, 0). For a walk that ends on its start mark, the distance of the last pose from the origin is the drift of Point-LIO.

Parameters

All are read-only, read once at start-up.

voxel_sizedelta_rate_hzpose_rate_hzfull_map_rate_hzoutput_dirsave_on_exitParameter0.052.010.00.0emptyfalseDefault0.052.010.00.0set by the launch filetrueIn map_builder.yamlm. Side of a cube. Must be above 0How often the new cubes are sent. Above 0How often the pose is sent. Above 0The whole map on a topic. 0 is offFolder for the runs. Empty makes save failSave when you press Ctrl-CMeaning

Topics and services

ininoutoutoutserviceserviceDirectioncloudodom/map_builder/delta/map_builder/pose/map_builder/full_map/map_builder/get_map/map_builder/saveNamesensor_msgs/PointCloud2nav_msgs/Odometrygo2_mapping_msgs/MapDeltageometry_msgs/PoseStampedsensor_msgs/PointCloud2go2_mapping_msgs/GetMapstd_srvs/TriggerTypereliable, queue 100reliable, queue 100reliable, queue 25reliable, queue 1reliable, transient local, queue 1. Only if the rate is above 0QoS

Transient local means a viewer that connects late still gets the last map. Turn full_map_rate_hz on only to look at the map in RViz: every message holds the whole map.

Build and test

	cd ~/unitree_go2
	source ~/unitree_ros2/setup.sh
	vcs import src < go2.repos
	colcon build --packages-up-to map_builder

It needs PCL (the point cloud library) for the PCD file. The package has no unit tests yet. It was checked by replaying a bag through the whole chain on the laptop. The steps are in src/map_builder/README.md. A correct run of 2026-10-19_line_01 at -r 0.25 gives:

Points in map.pcdLines in trajectory.tumx of the last poseros2 run map_builder voxel_count <map.pcd> 0.05Last seqCheck44,641 and 44,729 in two runs2975.33 to 5.35 m, the tape says 5.40 msecond inserted: 0about 150, depends on timingReal result

If the map has about 18,700 points and the end is at x 7.36 m, Point-LIO ran with the old 0.5 m filter size. Check filter_size_surf and filter_size_map in point_lio.yaml.

Common problems

another map builder is running, then the node stopssave answers map is emptyFrame ID mismatch: expected camera_initSymptomAn old map_builder is still aliveNo scan arrivedSomething else publishes on /cloud_registeredCausepgrep -af map_builder, stop it, start againCheck ros2 topic hz /cloud_registeredros2 topic info -v /cloud_registeredFix

Known gaps

- No unit tests. VoxelMap, Trajectory and map_io are plain C++ and easy to test. The CMake file has the lines ready but commented out. The only checks are the bag replay and voxel_count.
- The first point of a cube stays, the rest are lost. There is no average. A noisy first point stays in the map for the whole run.
- Nothing is ever removed. A person who walks through the scene leaves points that stay in the map. Point-LIO has no loop closing either, so drift is not corrected later.
- A pose can be published and not saved. on_odometry ignores the answer of Trajectory::add. A pose that is not newer than the last is skipped in the file but still goes to /map_builder/pose.
- A save is lost if the node is killed. The map is only in memory. save_on_exit works on Ctrl-C. A crash or kill -9 loses the run, unless save was called before.
- A scan with another frame is dropped with a warning only. The warning comes at most every 2 s.
- Two nodes starting together. The check counts publishers after 2 s. From reading the code, not from a test, two nodes that start together could both see two and both stop.
